top_choice_rationale: Circuit QED (Blais, Wallraff, Schoelkopf), worded narrowly as strong coupling of a single microwave photon to a superconducting artificial atom plus dispersive readout, is a sharply dated, twenty-year-reproduced result that is physically distinct from the 2025 macroscopic-tunnelling prize. Its main weaknesses, the Girvin and Huang credit boundary and the sequencing after 2025, are real but manageable with a narrow citation. P002 (optical lattice clock, Katori and Ye) is the cleaner two-name credit and a close second, ahead of the Higgs trio, whose three-name credit cannot represent two collaborations without excluding serious claimants, but which still beats no award.
recusal_note: I direct WACQT at Chalmers, which builds superconducting processors based on circuit QED, and work in this field with Chalmers colleagues Per Delsing and C. M. Wilson; Chalmers also hosted researchers associated with the 2025 prize. No documented tie to Blais, Wallraff, Schoelkopf, Katori, Ye or the Higgs candidates; a recusal question could arise for P001.
